acme.text:
Symptom: CI/CD pipeline or build platform reports 'Error: Build exceeded the time limit of 45 minutes', 'Build timed out', or 'Job exceeded maximum execution time'. The build process is killed before completing.

Root Cause: Build step contains an infinite loop or hung process, test suite running integration tests that require external services (not mocked), Webpack/Next.js bundle optimization taking excessive time due to large dependencies, or build machine is underpowered for the workload.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Check build logs for the last step before timeout — it shows where the hang occurred
2. Run build locally with timing: 'time npm run build'
3. Check for accidental network calls in build scripts that await responses from down services
4. Profile webpack: add 'speed-measure-webpack-plugin' to identify slow loaders

Fix:
- Optimize bundle: enable tree-shaking, lazy loading, and code splitting in next.config.js
- Increase timeout for legitimate long builds: update CI config (GitHub Actions: timeout-minutes: 60)
- Fix infinite loops: search for 'while(true)' or recursive calls without base cases in build scripts
- Mock external services in test phase: set TEST_MODE=true to skip integration calls
- Split build into parallel jobs: build frontend and backend concurrently
- For Acme Vercel builds: check Vercel > Project > Settings > Build & Development > Build Command timeout
- Use caching: cache node_modules between CI runs (actions/cache@v3)

Prevention: Set explicit timeouts on all async operations; profile builds monthly; set alerts if build time exceeds 20 minutes.

metadata.title: Build Exceeded Time Limit / Build Timeout

acme.text:
Symptom: Build or runtime fails with 'Cannot find module \'<package-name>\'' or 'npm ERR! 404 Not Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/<package>' or 'Error: Cannot find module' in Node.js.

Root Cause: package.json lists a dependency that is not installed (node_modules missing or outdated), private package registry misconfigured, or a package was removed from npm registry.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Check error message for the exact module name
2. Verify package.json contains the dependency under 'dependencies' or 'devDependencies'
3. Check if node_modules directory exists and contains the package
4. For CI: confirm cache is not stale — force clean install

Fix:
- Run 'npm install' in the project root to install all listed dependencies
- If package is missing from package.json: 'npm install <package-name> --save'
- For Acme private packages: ensure .npmrc contains 'registry=https://npm.acme-internal.io' and NPM_TOKEN env var is set
- Clear corrupted cache: 'npm cache clean --force && rm -rf node_modules && npm install'
- In CI (GitHub Actions): ensure 'actions/setup-node' step runs before build step
- Check package-lock.json is committed and matches package.json

Prevention: Pin dependency versions; use 'npm ci' in CI for reproducible installs; set up Dependabot alerts.

metadata.title: npm Dependency Not Found / Module Resolution Failure

acme.text:
Symptom: Application fails to start with 'Error: Missing required environment variable: <VAR_NAME>', 'undefined is not a valid value', or the build process exits early because a required configuration value is absent.

Root Cause: Environment variable not configured in deployment platform (Vercel, Kubernetes, Docker), .env file missing or not loaded, or variable name mismatch (typo, case sensitivity).

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Identify which variable is missing from the error message
2. Check .env.example for the full list of required variables
3. Verify the variable is set in the deployment target: 'printenv | grep VAR_NAME'
4. For Vercel: check Project Settings > Environment Variables for each environment (Production, Preview, Development)

Fix:
- Local development: copy .env.example to .env and fill in values: 'cp .env.example .env'
- Vercel: add variable via dashboard or CLI: 'vercel env add VAR_NAME'
- Kubernetes: add to ConfigMap or Secret and mount as env in Deployment spec
- Docker: pass via -e flag or --env-file option
- For Acme CI: add secrets to GitHub repository Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions

Common Acme Variables: DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, ACME_API_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE, SENTRY_DSN.

Prevention: Use a startup validation script (src/validateEnv.js) that checks all required vars at boot and fails fast with a clear error listing all missing vars.

metadata.title: Missing Environment Variable Causes Build or Runtime Failure

acme.text:
Symptom: The application crashes with 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' or 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded'. This occurs when the JVM cannot allocate an object because the heap is full and garbage collection is unable to free enough memory.

Root Cause: Insufficient JVM heap size configured for the workload, memory leak in application code retaining object references, or sudden spike in concurrent users/requests exceeding normal memory baseline.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Check application logs for 'OutOfMemoryError' stack trace
2. Review heap size settings: -Xms (initial) and -Xmx (maximum)
3. Inspect GC logs for excessive collection frequency
4. Use heap dump analysis (jmap -dump or -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError) to identify retained objects

Fix:
- Increase heap: add -Xmx2g (or appropriate size) to JVM_OPTS in Dockerfile or deployment config
- For Acme deployments: update JAVA_OPTS in acme-web-app/config/jvm.properties
- Check for memory leaks: static collections growing unboundedly, unclosed streams, event listener accumulation
- Add -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/var/log/heapdump.hprof for future diagnostics
- Monitor with: kubectl top pods -n acme-prod

Prevention: Set resource limits in Kubernetes manifests; configure alerting on heap usage > 80%.

metadata.title: OutOfMemory Error: Java Heap Space Exhaustion

acme.text:
Symptom: Server fails to start with 'Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000' (or other port number). The process cannot bind to the requested port because another process is already listening on it.

Root Cause: A previous instance of the application did not shut down cleanly (zombie process), another service on the same machine is using the port, or a development server was not terminated before restarting.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Identify which port is in conflict from the error message
2. Find the process occupying the port:
   - Linux/Mac: 'lsof -i :<PORT>' or 'ss -tlnp | grep <PORT>'
   - Windows: 'netstat -ano | findstr :<PORT>'
3. Check the PID of the occupying process

Fix:
- Kill the process using the port:
  - Linux/Mac: 'kill -9 <PID>' or 'npx kill-port <PORT>'
  - Windows: 'taskkill /F /PID <PID>'
- Change the application port via environment variable: PORT=3001 npm start
- For Acme deployments: update PORT in .env or Kubernetes Service targetPort
- In Docker: map to a different host port: '-p 3001:3000'

If this happens repeatedly in CI: add a pre-test step to kill any lingering processes on the target port.

Prevention: Use process managers (PM2, supervisord) with proper signal handling; implement graceful shutdown (process.on('SIGTERM', ...)).

globex.text:
Symptom: Globex CI pipeline (Jenkins/GitLab CI) reports 'Pipeline exceeded maximum duration of 60 minutes', 'Stage timed out after 30m', or build agent is terminated mid-run. Artifact is not produced; deployment does not proceed.

Root Cause: Integration test suite awaiting real external service (Kafka, database) that is unavailable in CI; large Docker image build without layer caching; Globex data migration script processing unexpectedly large dataset; network-dependent step waiting on a connection that never arrives.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Check Jenkins/GitLab build log for the last output line before timeout — this is where execution stalled
2. Look for lines like 'Waiting for connection...' or test names that never output a result
3. Check if the build consumed full timeout (60m) or a stage limit
4. Run the failing step locally with 'time' prefix to get baseline duration

Fix:
- Mock external services in CI: set GLOBEX_TEST_MODE=integration_mock to use Testcontainers or WireMock
- Enable Docker BuildKit cache: add DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 and --cache-from to docker build commands
- Globex Jenkins: increase pipeline timeout in Jenkinsfile: options { timeout(time: 90, unit: 'MINUTES') }
- GitLab CI: set timeout in .gitlab-ci.yml: timeout: 90 minutes per job
- Fix stalled tests: add per-test timeout annotations (@pytest.mark.timeout(60) or jest.setTimeout(30000))
- For data migration: batch process with LIMIT/OFFSET and checkpoint resume

Prevention: Set explicit timeouts on all external calls; run long jobs as scheduled pipelines (not on every commit); use Globex pipeline analytics dashboard to track build time trends.

metadata.title: Build or Pipeline Timeout in Globex CI/CD

globex.text:
Symptom: Globex CI pipeline fails with 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named \'<package>\'' (Python) or 'Cannot find module \'<package>\'' (Node.js). Deployment fails because a required library is not installed in the runtime environment.

Root Cause: requirements.txt or package.json not updated after adding a new import; Docker image built from cached layer that predates the new dependency; virtual environment not activated in CI step.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Check the failed import in the error — identify the package name
2. Search requirements.txt (Python) or package.json (Node): 'grep -r <package> requirements*.txt'
3. For Docker: check if the failing step runs BEFORE the 'pip install -r requirements.txt' layer
4. Verify the package name on PyPI vs the import name (e.g., 'Pillow' installs as 'PIL')

Fix:
- Python: add package to requirements.txt and rebuild: 'pip install -r requirements.txt'
- Node.js: 'npm install <package> --save' and commit package-lock.json
- Globex Docker builds: invalidate cache with --no-cache flag for the dependency layer
- For Globex private PyPI: add to ~/.pip/pip.conf: index-url = https://pypi.globex-internal.net/simple
- Ensure GLOBEX_PYPI_TOKEN is set in CI secrets
- Use 'pip freeze > requirements.txt' after local development to capture exact versions

Prevention: Automate dependency audits with pip-audit; use Dependabot for both Python and Node; require PR reviewers to check requirements files.

metadata.title: Missing Python Package or npm Module in Globex CI

globex.text:
Symptom: Globex service startup fails with 'KeyError: \'<VAR_NAME>\'' (Python) or 'Error: Environment variable <VAR_NAME> is required but not set'. Health check fails immediately after deploy. Kubernetes pod enters CrashLoopBackOff.

Root Cause: New environment variable added to code but not provisioned in Kubernetes Secret or ConfigMap; staging environment missing a variable that exists in production; variable renamed in a refactor but old name still referenced.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Check the CrashLoopBackOff logs: 'kubectl logs <pod> -n globex-prod --previous'
2. List currently set env vars in running pod: 'kubectl exec <pod> -- env | sort'
3. Compare against .env.example or Globex environment manifest at infra/k8s/envs/
4. Check if the variable exists in the correct namespace Secret: 'kubectl get secret globex-app-secrets -o yaml'

Fix:
- Add missing variable to Kubernetes Secret: 'kubectl create secret generic globex-app-secrets --from-literal=<VAR>=<VALUE> --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -'
- For ConfigMap (non-sensitive): edit infra/k8s/envs/configmap.yaml and apply
- Globex AWS ECS: add via AWS Console > ECS > Task Definition > Environment Variables or update Terraform
- Rollback: if urgent, roll back to previous deployment: 'kubectl rollout undo deployment/globex-api -n globex-prod'

Globex Required Variables: GLOBEX_DB_URL, GLOBEX_REDIS_CLUSTER, GLOBEX_KAFKA_BROKERS, GLOBEX_S3_BUCKET, GLOBEX_VAULT_ADDR.

Prevention: Use globex-config-validator pre-deploy hook; document all variables in infra/k8s/envs/README.md.

metadata.title: Missing Environment Variable in Globex Deployment

globex.text:
Symptom: Globex microservice crashes with 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' or Python process killed with 'MemoryError' / OS OOM killer log entry ('Out of memory: Kill process <PID>'). Kubernetes pod restarts with OOMKilled reason.

Root Cause: JVM or Python process heap limit too low for current data volume; unbounded in-memory cache growing during high-traffic periods; large dataset loaded fully into memory instead of streamed.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Run 'kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n globex-prod' — look for 'OOMKilled' in Last State
2. Check pod memory usage: 'kubectl top pod <pod-name> -n globex-prod'
3. For Java: review GC logs, enable with -Xlog:gc*:file=/var/log/gc.log
4. For Python: use memory_profiler or tracemalloc to identify large allocations

Fix:
- Java: increase heap -Xmx4g in Globex Helm values: globex-services/helm/values.yaml under jvmOptions
- Python: increase pod memory limit in Kubernetes: resources.limits.memory: 2Gi
- Fix unbounded cache: add TTL and max-size to Globex CacheManager (see internal wiki: Cache Configuration)
- Stream large datasets instead of loading fully: use pandas read_csv(chunksize=10000) or Java streaming APIs
- Globex-specific: check the ReportGenerationJob — it accumulates report rows in memory; use temp DB tables

Prevention: Set Kubernetes resource requests and limits; configure HPA to scale before OOM; alert on memory > 85%.

metadata.title: OutOfMemory Error: Heap Exhaustion in Globex Services

globex.text:
Symptom: Globex service or test runner fails with 'Error: listen EADDRINUSE :::8080' or 'bind: address already in use' (Go). Port binding fails and service cannot start, causing health checks to fail and downstream services to report connection refused.

Root Cause: Parallel CI jobs using the same port on a shared runner; previous test suite did not release port after completion; Docker container from previous run still occupying host port; Globex gateway running on same port as a new microservice.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. In CI: check if parallel job matrix shares the same runner and port
2. Find occupying process: 'ss -tlnp | grep 8080' or 'netstat -tlnp | grep 8080'
3. Check Docker: 'docker ps | grep 8080'
4. For Go services: check for missing listener.Close() in service shutdown

Fix:
- Kill process: 'fuser -k 8080/tcp' (Linux) or 'kill $(lsof -t -i:8080)'
- For CI: use dynamic port allocation — set PORT=0 and let OS assign, then read assigned port from service startup log
- Docker: 'docker stop $(docker ps -q --filter publish=8080)'
- Globex microservices: each service has a default port in globex-services/config/ports.yaml — resolve conflicts there
- Use Globex service mesh (Envoy): all inter-service calls go through mesh, avoid direct port binding conflicts

Prevention: Assign dedicated port ranges per service in Globex port registry; use Docker Compose with fixed port mappings; integrate port-conflict-check in pre-commit hooks.

metadata.title: Port Conflict: EADDRINUSE in Globex Local and CI Environments
